--- ## Why `some-divide-and-conquer`? Single-agent coding workflows break down on large specifications: context windows fill up with compiler noise, sequential task execution takes hours, unreviewed commits introduce regressions, and local status files (`KANBAN.md`) create endless merge conflicts. **`some-divide-and-conquer`** is a **language-, framework-, and product-agnostic** Google Antigravity, Claude Code, and OpenAI Codex plugin by **[Some(CS)](https://github.com/some-of-cs)** that turns any monolithic specification into a self-governing, parallel multi-agent software factory: 1. **Monolithic Docs $\to$ Modules $\to$ User Stories $\to$ Dynamic $K$ Implementation Units**: - Systematically decomposes huge PRDs, RFCs, or research documents into bounded **Modules**, cohesive **User Stories**, and a **dynamically calculated number ($K \in [1, N]$) of pure-implementation vertical slices** using a quantitative **Unit Sizing Decision Matrix**. 2. **100% Parallel, Non-Blocking Execution in Isolated `.worktrees/`**: - Every Implementation Unit is a **pure implementation slice** (never a validation-only unit waiting on siblings) with orthogonal file/module boundaries so **all $K$ units run simultaneously in parallel** inside `.worktrees/`. 3. **Concurrent Multi-Council Code Review & Mandatory `patch-implementer` Loop**: - Multiple independent **Code Reviewing Councils** run in parallel across Units, Stories, and Modules—auditing **Gate G0** (build/lint), **Gate G1** (test coverage), **Gate G2** (`security-audit`), **Gate G-Complexity** (`cyclomatic-complexity`), and **Gate G-Docs**. - Story and Module Leaders **never fix code directly in their own context**; any issue flagged by a Council automatically spawns an isolated **`patch-implementer`** subagent (`patch/*` branch & PR) in a continuous self-correction loop until 0 issues remain. 4. **GitHub Projects Visual Kanban & In-PR Conversation Audit Trail (Zero Local Report/Kanban Clutter)**: - Development status (`Todo`, `In Progress`, `In Review / PR Open`, `Merged`) is tracked visually in **GitHub Projects** (`gh project`) alongside a local `.agents/checkpoints//checkpoint.json`. - All Implementation Reports, Security Audits, Cyclomatic Complexity tables, and Council Sign-Offs are posted **directly as comments inside the GitHub Pull Request conversation (`gh pr comment`)** rather than cluttering the repository with local report files. 5. **Pluggable 283-Agent Specialist Roster ([`msitarzewski/agency-agents`](https://github.com/msitarzewski/agency-agents))**: - Choose the exact specialists your project needs from **all 18 divisions and 283 agents** of `msitarzewski/agency-agents`—whether you are building a Rust SDK, a TypeScript/React SaaS, a Python AI pipeline, a Go microservice, a mobile app, or a Unity/Unreal game. --- ## Token Consumption & Gemini Flash Family Optimization > [!IMPORTANT] > ### High Code Quality vs. High Token Consumption (Designed for the Gemini Flash Family) > - **Extreme Output Quality**: By running $K$ parallel Unit Implementers, multiple concurrent Code Reviewing Councils (`security-audit` + `cyclomatic-complexity`), and automated `patch-implementer` remediation loops across every tier, this plugin produces **exceptionally high-quality, zero-warning, production-grade code and products**. > - **High Token Consumption Trade-Off**: Because every unit, patch, story, and module undergoes full independent multi-agent implementation and multi-council verification, **this workflow consumes a large volume of tokens**. > - **Primary Target — Gemini Flash Family**: This plugin is **mainly developed, tuned, and recommended for the Gemini Flash family** (such as `gemini-2.5-flash` and `gemini-3-flash`), which delivers the high speed, large context window, and token cost-efficiency required for parallel multi-agent swarms. > - **Single-Profile Operation with `quota-sentinel`**: This plugin operates on **one profile at a time**. A dedicated autonomous **`quota-sentinel`** monitors token velocity and rate limits (`429` / `1%` remaining capacity), automatically flushing state to `.agents/checkpoints//checkpoint.json`, pausing active agents, and scheduling an automatic wakeup timer until your quota resets. --- ## Prerequisites: Mandatory `git` & `gh` Preflight Gate Before the plugin starts any decomposition, worktree provisioning, or agent spawning, **Gate 0 (`scripts/preflight-check.sh`)** verifies that both **`git`** and **`gh` (GitHub CLI)** exist on `$PATH` and are authenticated: | Prerequisite | Minimum Version | Why It Is Required Before Starting | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **`git`** | `>= 2.30` | Provisions isolated `.worktrees/` for parallel Module, Story, Unit, and Patch agents. | | **`gh` (GitHub CLI)** | `>= 2.30` | Creates PRs (`gh pr create`), posts in-conversation reports (`gh pr comment`), syncs GitHub Projects Kanban (`gh project`), and executes cascading merges (`gh pr merge`). | Verify your environment at any time: ```bash ./scripts/preflight-check.sh ``` *(This check also runs automatically on `SessionStart` via [`hooks.json`](hooks.json). If either `git` or `gh` is missing, the plugin halts immediately before spawning any agents.)* --- ## From Monolithic Docs to Non-Blocking Implementation Units The [`spec-decomposition`](skills/spec-decomposition/SKILL.md) skill provides a formal 4-level pipeline to turn any monolithic specification into parallel execution units: ```mermaid flowchart TD Doc["Level 0: Monolithic Spec / PRD / RFC / Research Doc"] --> Mod1["Level 1: Module 1 (feat/module-1-...)"] Doc --> Mod2["Level 1: Module 2 (feat/module-2-...)"] Doc --> ModM["Level 1: Module M (feat/module-M-...)"] Mod1 --> Story1["Level 2: User Story 1.1 (feat/us-1.1.0-...)"] Mod1 --> Story2["Level 2: User Story 1.2 (feat/us-1.2.0-...)"] Story1 --> U1["Level 3: Unit 1 (feat/us-1.1.0/unit-1-...)"] Story1 --> U2["Level 3: Unit 2 (feat/us-1.1.0/unit-2-...)"] Story1 --> UK["Level 3: Unit K (feat/us-1.1.0/unit-K-...)"] ``` ### Dynamic Implementation Unit Sizing Matrix ($K$ Is Not Fixed at 5) Implementation units per User Story **do not have to be 5**—a story can require fewer (e.g., 2 or 3) or more (e.g., 6, 7, or 8+) depending on its complexity and surface area. Calculate the **Story Decomposition Score ($S_{\text{story}}$)**: | Dimension | Weight | Score = `1` (Low) | Score = `2` (Medium) | Score = `3` (High) | Score = `4` (Very High) | | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **$D_1$: Entities / Endpoints / Components** | **35%** | 1–2 items | 3–4 items | 5–6 items | 7+ items | | **$D_2$: Estimated Production LOC** | **25%** | $< 300$ LOC | $300 - 700$ LOC | $700 - 1,400$ LOC | $> 1,400$ LOC | | **$D_3$: Algorithmic / Protocol Complexity** | **20%** | Simple CRUD / UI | Validation / state machine | Crypto / streaming / dual-protocol | Concurrency / distributed state | | **$D_4$: Natural Orthogonal Boundaries** | **20%** | 1–2 files/modules | 3–4 independent files/modules | 5–6 independent files/modules | 7+ independent files/modules | $$S_{\text{story}} = 0.35 D_1 + 0.25 D_2 + 0.20 D_3 + 0.20 D_4$$ | Story Score ($S_{\text{story}}$) | Recommended Units ($K$) | Typical Story Profile | | :---: | :---: | :--- | | **$1.00 - 1.25$** | **1–2 Units** | Compact config, utility, or 2-component slice ($150-250$ LOC/unit) | | **$1.26 - 2.00$** | **3 Units** | Focused domain model + service + handler/controller slice | | **$2.01 - 2.55$** | **4 Units** | Medium multi-endpoint or full-stack feature slice | | **$2.56 - 3.10$** | **5 Units** | Rich domain story (models, CRUD, streaming/pagination, lifecycle actions) | | **$3.11 - 3.55$** | **6–7 Units** | Large subsystem spanning 6–7 orthogonal submodules | | **$3.56 - 4.00$** | **8+ Units (or Split Story)** | Mega-story: partition into 8 parallel units or split into two User Stories | ### Two Non-Negotiable Unit Design Invariants 1. **Pure Deliverable Production Only (Zero Validation-Only Units)**: - Every unit $1..K$ MUST produce real primary artifacts (source code + unit tests in software; drafted sections, models, or campaign assets + self-checks in non-software). - **Never** create a unit whose purpose is *"Unit $K$: Write integration tests or validate Units $1..(K-1)$"*. Story-level integration testing is performed by the Story Leader after all $K$ units merge. 2. **Zero Inter-Unit Blocking (100% Parallel Execution)**: - Units $1..K$ own disjoint files/submodules (with any shared interfaces seeded on the story branch first) so **all $K$ Unit Implementers run simultaneously in parallel** without waiting on one another. --- ## Parallel Execution, Multi-Council Review & `patch-implementer` Loop ```mermaid flowchart TD SL["Story Leader (1m Watchdog)"] --> U1["Unit 1 Implementer (.worktrees/unit-1)"] SL --> U2["Unit 2 Implementer (.worktrees/unit-2)"] SL --> UK["Unit K Implementer (.worktrees/unit-K)"] U1 --> C1["Unit 1 Code Reviewing Council"] U2 --> C2["Unit 2 Code Reviewing Council"] UK --> CK["Unit K Code Reviewing Council"] C1 --> Q["Cascading gh pr merge (1 -> 2 -> ... -> K) into Story Branch"] C2 --> Q CK --> Q Q --> SC["Story-Level Code Reviewing Council"] SC -- "Issues Flagged" --> PI["Spawn Dedicated patch-implementer (patch/us-M.S.0-*)"] PI -- "PR Reviewed & Merged via gh pr merge" --> SC SC -- "100% Clean Sign-Off" --> MP["Merge Story PR into Module Branch via gh pr merge"] ``` ### How the 3-Tier Review & `patch-implementer` Loop Works 1. **Parallel Unit Councils**: - Each Unit Implementer ($1..K$) invokes its own independent **Code Reviewing Council** in parallel as soon as its PR opens. If any issue or high complexity ($CC > 10$) is found, the Unit Implementer fixes it and re-invokes the Council until `GATE G-REVIEW APPROVED` is posted in the PR conversation. 2. **Story-Level Review & Mandatory `patch-implementer`**: - Once Units $1..K$ merge into `feat/us-M.S.0-`, the Story Leader opens the Story PR and invokes a fresh Story-level **Code Reviewing Council**. - **Strict Invariant**: If ANY issue is found at the story level, the **Story Leader NEVER fixes code directly in its own context**. It spawns a dedicated **`patch-implementer`** subagent in `.worktrees/patch-us-M.S.0-`, opens a Patch PR, merges it into the story branch via `gh pr merge`, and re-invokes the Story Council until 0 problems remain. 3. **Module-Level Review & Mandatory `patch-implementer`**: - Once all User Stories merge into `feat/module-M-`, the Module Leader invokes a Module-level **Code Reviewing Council**. Any findings trigger a dedicated **`patch-implementer`** on `patch/module-M-` until 100% clean sign-off is achieved. 4. **End-of-Module Whole-Codebase Validation**: - After the Module PR merges into `main`, the Main Supervisor runs the entire repository's test suite, linter, formatter, and doctests across Modules $1..M$ with a Whole-Codebase Gatekeeper Council. --- ## Bundled Reviewing Council & a **Universal Tri-Platform Plugin (`some-divide-and-conquer`)** ready for direct publishing and installation across **Google Antigravity**, **Claude Code**, and **OpenAI Codex CLI**. ### Option A: Google Antigravity Marketplace / CLI (`agy`) 1. **Native Antigravity Plugin Manifest**: [`plugin.json`](plugin.json) (with [`hooks.json`](hooks.json) and [`rules/AGENTS.md`](rules/AGENTS.md)). 2. **Install into any workspace**: ```bash git clone https://github.com/some-of-cs/some-divide-and-conquer.git some-divide-and-conquer ./some-divide-and-conquer/scripts/install-plugin.sh \ --tool antigravity \ --target /path/to/your/project \ --divisions engineering,security,testing ``` ### Option B: Claude Code Plugin Marketplace (`/plugin`) 1. **Native Claude Code Manifests**: [`.claude-plugin/plugin.json`](.claude-plugin/plugin.json) and [`.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`](.claude-plugin/marketplace.json). 2. **Install directly from the Claude Code Marketplace**: ```text your agent (or run `/divide-and-conquer docs/SPECIFICATION.md`): ```text Using the some-divide-and-conquer plugin rules and the spec-decomposition skill: 1. Execute Module 1 by spawning parallel Story Leaders and Unit Implementers in .worktrees/, running parallel Code Reviewing Councils, using patch-implementer for any review findings, and posting all execution and review reports directly to the GitHub PR conversations. ``` --- ## Real-World Case Study: `some-stripe` (`v0.8.0`) See [`examples/some-stripe/`](examples/some-stripe/README.md) for the complete case study of how **[`some-stripe`](https://github.com/some-of-cs/some-stripe)**—an idiomatic Rust 2024 SDK and constant-time webhook engine for Stripe API v1 & v2—was built from a single monolithic research document using this exact workflow: - **Input**: 1 monolithic specification (`Stripe Services and API Research.md`) - **Output**: **8 Modules**, **16 User Stories**, **80 Parallel Implementation Units**, and **137 merged GitHub PRs** - **Quality**: **705+ unit/wire tests**, **220+ runnable doctests**, **0 compiler/Clippy warnings**, **Max Cyclomatic Complexity $CC \le 6$** on primary paths, and **100% Gate G2 / Gate G-Law compliance**. --- ## Why `some-divide-and-conquer`? Single-agent coding workflows break down on large specifications: context windows fill up with compiler noise, sequential task execution takes hours, unreviewed commits introduce regressions, and local status files (`KANBAN.md`) create endless merge conflicts. **`some-divide-and-conquer`** is a **language-, framework-, and product-agnostic** Google Antigravity, Claude Code, and OpenAI Codex plugin by **[Some(CS)](https://github.com/some-of-cs)** that turns any monolithic specification into a self-governing, parallel multi-agent software factory: 1. **Monolithic Docs $\to$ Modules $\to$ User Stories $\to$ Dynamic $K$ Implementation Units**: - Systematically decomposes huge PRDs, RFCs, or research documents into bounded **Modules**, cohesive **User Stories**, and a **dynamically calculated number ($K \in [1, N]$) of pure-implementation vertical slices** using a quantitative **Unit Sizing Decision Matrix**. 2. **100% Parallel, Non-Blocking Execution in Isolated `.worktrees/`**: - Every Implementation Unit is a **pure implementation slice** (never a validation-only unit waiting on siblings) with orthogonal file/module boundaries so **all $K$ units run simultaneously in parallel** inside `.worktrees/`. 3. **Concurrent Multi-Council Code Review & Mandatory `patch-implementer` Loop**: - Multiple independent **Code Reviewing Councils** run in parallel across Units, Stories, and Modules—auditing **Gate G0** (build/lint), **Gate G1** (test coverage), **Gate G2** (`security-audit`), **Gate G-Complexity** (`cyclomatic-complexity`), and **Gate G-Docs**. - Story and Module Leaders **never fix code directly in their own context**; any issue flagged by a Council automatically spawns an isolated **`patch-implementer`** subagent (`patch/*` branch & PR) in a continuous self-correction loop until 0 issues remain. 4. **GitHub Projects Visual Kanban & In-PR Conversation Audit Trail (Zero Local Report/Kanban Clutter)**: - Development status (`Todo`, `In Progress`, `In Review / PR Open`, `Merged`) is tracked visually in **GitHub Projects** (`gh project`) alongside a local `.agents/checkpoints//checkpoint.json`. - All Implementation Reports, Security Audits, Cyclomatic Complexity tables, and Council Sign-Offs are posted **directly as comments inside the GitHub Pull Request conversation (`gh pr comment`)** rather than cluttering the repository with local report files. 5. **Pluggable 283-Agent Specialist Roster ([`msitarzewski/agency-agents`](https://github.com/msitarzewski/agency-agents))**: - Choose the exact specialists your project needs from **all 18 divisions and 283 agents** of `msitarzewski/agency-agents`—whether you are building a Rust SDK, a TypeScript/React SaaS, a Python AI pipeline, a Go microservice, a mobile app, or a Unity/Unreal game. --- ## Token Consumption & Gemini Flash Family Optimization > [!IMPORTANT] > ### High Code Quality vs. High Token Consumption (Designed for the Gemini Flash Family) > - **Extreme Output Quality**: By running $K$ parallel Unit Implementers, multiple concurrent Code Reviewing Councils (`security-audit` + `cyclomatic-complexity`), and automated `patch-implementer` remediation loops across every tier, this plugin produces **exceptionally high-quality, zero-warning, production-grade code and products**. > - **High Token Consumption Trade-Off**: Because every unit, patch, story, and module undergoes full independent multi-agent implementation and multi-council verification, **this workflow consumes a large volume of tokens**. > - **Primary Target — Gemini Flash Family**: This plugin is **mainly developed, tuned, and recommended for the Gemini Flash family** (such as `gemini-2.5-flash` and `gemini-3-flash`), which delivers the high speed, large context window, and token cost-efficiency required for parallel multi-agent swarms. > - **Single-Profile Operation with `quota-sentinel`**: This plugin operates on **one profile at a time**. A dedicated autonomous **`quota-sentinel`** monitors token velocity and rate limits (`429` / `1%` remaining capacity), automatically flushing state to `.agents/checkpoints//checkpoint.json`, pausing active agents, and scheduling an automatic wakeup timer until your quota resets. --- ## Prerequisites: Mandatory `git` & `gh` Preflight Gate Before the plugin starts any decomposition, worktree provisioning, or agent spawning, **Gate 0 (`scripts/preflight-check.sh`)** verifies that both **`git`** and **`gh` (GitHub CLI)** exist on `$PATH` and are authenticated: | Prerequisite | Minimum Version | Why It Is Required Before Starting | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **`git`** | `>= 2.30` | Provisions isolated `.worktrees/` for parallel Module, Story, Unit, and Patch agents. | | **`gh` (GitHub CLI)** | `>= 2.30` | Creates PRs (`gh pr create`), posts in-conversation reports (`gh pr comment`), syncs GitHub Projects Kanban (`gh project`), and executes cascading merges (`gh pr merge`). | Verify your environment at any time: ```bash ./scripts/preflight-check.sh ``` *(This check also runs automatically on `SessionStart` via [`hooks.json`](hooks.json). If either `git` or `gh` is missing, the plugin halts immediately before spawning any agents.)* --- ## From Monolithic Docs to Non-Blocking Implementation Units The [`spec-decomposition`](skills/spec-decomposition/SKILL.md) skill provides a formal 4-level pipeline to turn any monolithic specification into parallel execution units: ```mermaid flowchart TD Doc["Level 0: Monolithic Spec / PRD / RFC / Research Doc"] --> Mod1["Level 1: Module 1 (feat/module-1-...)"] Doc --> Mod2["Level 1: Module 2 (feat/module-2-...)"] Doc --> ModM["Level 1: Module M (feat/module-M-...)"] Mod1 --> Story1["Level 2: User Story 1.1 (feat/us-1.1.0-...)"] Mod1 --> Story2["Level 2: User Story 1.2 (feat/us-1.2.0-...)"] Story1 --> U1["Level 3: Unit 1 (feat/us-1.1.0/unit-1-...)"] Story1 --> U2["Level 3: Unit 2 (feat/us-1.1.0/unit-2-...)"] Story1 --> UK["Level 3: Unit K (feat/us-1.1.0/unit-K-...)"] ``` ### Dynamic Implementation Unit Sizing Matrix ($K$ Is Not Fixed at 5) Implementation units per User Story **do not have to be 5**—a story can require fewer (e.g., 2 or 3) or more (e.g., 6, 7, or 8+) depending on its complexity and surface area. Calculate the **Story Decomposition Score ($S_{\text{story}}$)**: | Dimension | Weight | Score = `1` (Low) | Score = `2` (Medium) | Score = `3` (High) | Score = `4` (Very High) | | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **$D_1$: Entities / Endpoints / Components** | **35%** | 1–2 items | 3–4 items | 5–6 items | 7+ items | | **$D_2$: Estimated Production LOC** | **25%** | $< 300$ LOC | $300 - 700$ LOC | $700 - 1,400$ LOC | $> 1,400$ LOC | | **$D_3$: Algorithmic / Protocol Complexity** | **20%** | Simple CRUD / UI | Validation / state machine | Crypto / streaming / dual-protocol | Concurrency / distributed state | | **$D_4$: Natural Orthogonal Boundaries** | **20%** | 1–2 files/modules | 3–4 independent files/modules | 5–6 independent files/modules | 7+ independent files/modules | $$S_{\text{story}} = 0.35 D_1 + 0.25 D_2 + 0.20 D_3 + 0.20 D_4$$ | Story Score ($S_{\text{story}}$) | Recommended Units ($K$) | Typical Story Profile | | :---: | :---: | :--- | | **$1.00 - 1.25$** | **1–2 Units** | Compact config, utility, or 2-component slice ($150-250$ LOC/unit) | | **$1.26 - 2.00$** | **3 Units** | Focused domain model + service + handler/controller slice | | **$2.01 - 2.55$** | **4 Units** | Medium multi-endpoint or full-stack feature slice | | **$2.56 - 3.10$** | **5 Units** | Rich domain story (models, CRUD, streaming/pagination, lifecycle actions) | | **$3.11 - 3.55$** | **6–7 Units** | Large subsystem spanning 6–7 orthogonal submodules | | **$3.56 - 4.00$** | **8+ Units (or Split Story)** | Mega-story: partition into 8 parallel units or split into two User Stories | ### Two Non-Negotiable Unit Design Invariants 1. **Pure Deliverable Production Only (Zero Validation-Only Units)**: - Every unit $1..K$ MUST produce real primary artifacts (source code + unit tests in software; drafted sections, models, or campaign assets + self-checks in non-software). - **Never** create a unit whose purpose is *"Unit $K$: Write integration tests or validate Units $1..(K-1)$"*. Story-level integration testing is performed by the Story Leader after all $K$ units merge. 2. **Zero Inter-Unit Blocking (100% Parallel Execution)**: - Units $1..K$ own disjoint files/submodules (with any shared interfaces seeded on the story branch first) so **all $K$ Unit Implementers run simultaneously in parallel** without waiting on one another. --- ## Parallel Execution, Multi-Council Review & `patch-implementer` Loop ```mermaid flowchart TD SL["Story Leader (1m Watchdog)"] --> U1["Unit 1 Implementer (.worktrees/unit-1)"] SL --> U2["Unit 2 Implementer (.worktrees/unit-2)"] SL --> UK["Unit K Implementer (.worktrees/unit-K)"] U1 --> C1["Unit 1 Code Reviewing Council"] U2 --> C2["Unit 2 Code Reviewing Council"] UK --> CK["Unit K Code Reviewing Council"] C1 --> Q["Cascading gh pr merge (1 -> 2 -> ... -> K) into Story Branch"] C2 --> Q CK --> Q Q --> SC["Story-Level Code Reviewing Council"] SC -- "Issues Flagged" --> PI["Spawn Dedicated patch-implementer (patch/us-M.S.0-*)"] PI -- "PR Reviewed & Merged via gh pr merge" --> SC SC -- "100% Clean Sign-Off" --> MP["Merge Story PR into Module Branch via gh pr merge"] ``` ### How the 3-Tier Review & `patch-implementer` Loop Works 1. **Parallel Unit Councils**: - Each Unit Implementer ($1..K$) invokes its own independent **Code Reviewing Council** in parallel as soon as its PR opens. If any issue or high complexity ($CC > 10$) is found, the Unit Implementer fixes it and re-invokes the Council until `GATE G-REVIEW APPROVED` is posted in the PR conversation. 2. **Story-Level Review & Mandatory `patch-implementer`**: - Once Units $1..K$ merge into `feat/us-M.S.0-`, the Story Leader opens the Story PR and invokes a fresh Story-level **Code Reviewing Council**. - **Strict Invariant**: If ANY issue is found at the story level, the **Story Leader NEVER fixes code directly in its own context**. It spawns a dedicated **`patch-implementer`** subagent in `.worktrees/patch-us-M.S.0-`, opens a Patch PR, merges it into the story branch via `gh pr merge`, and re-invokes the Story Council until 0 problems remain. 3. **Module-Level Review & Mandatory `patch-implementer`**: - Once all User Stories merge into `feat/module-M-`, the Module Leader invokes a Module-level **Code Reviewing Council**. Any findings trigger a dedicated **`patch-implementer`** on `patch/module-M-` until 100% clean sign-off is achieved. 4. **End-of-Module Whole-Codebase Validation**: - After the Module PR merges into `main`, the Main Supervisor runs the entire repository's test suite, linter, formatter, and doctests across Modules $1..M$ with a Whole-Codebase Gatekeeper Council. --- ## Bundled Reviewing Council &
